messages:
alice: Heads up — over the last 48h we've seen steady RSS growth on the streaming chat worker when customers hit long tool loops (~20+ tool calls per session). Not a hard crash but ~10-12% growth per hour until OOM throttles.
ben: Yikes. Is it tied to KV cache size or allocator fragmentation?
alice: Initial diff shows KV cache entry count stable, but resident set keeps climbing. Heap profile shows lots of small retained chunks. Suspecting fragmentation + some entries not being released back to free bins.
carla: Can you paste the pprof snapshot and jemalloc stats?
dave: infra-bot re-deployed a debug build to one pool at 10:02 UTC, adding jemalloc stats and kv debug counters.
alice: Paste 10:05 snapshot (sampling):
```
pprof: top 10
  45.1MB  45.1MB  30.0%  30.0%  runtime.mallocgc
  23.4MB  23.4MB  15.6%  15.6%  github.com/redwood/serve/kv.(*Cache).Insert
  18.2MB  18.2MB  12.1%  12.1%  runtime.mcache refill
  12.0MB  12.0MB   8.0%   8.0%  github.com/redwood/serve/session.(*Session).AppendChunk
```
ben: Interesting that mallocgc + mcache are high — points to allocator churn/fragmentation.
carla: What's kv cache internals reporting? counts, evictions, reused entries?
alice: From /metrics/kv-debug at 10:06:
```
kv_total_entries 5123
kv_active_entries 4897
kv_evictions_total 178
kv_eviction_scan_ops 0
kv_reuse_hits 42
kv_page_faults 0
kv_fragmented_bytes 12648576
```
ben: Low reuse_hits suggests we rarely reassign freed slots. Fragmented_bytes looks non-trivial (12MB).
dave: I also captured jemalloc stats at 10:07:
```
allocated: 1.2G
active: 1.35G
metadata: 24M
resident: 1.6G
fragmentation: 250M
```
carla: Fragmentation 250M is big; maybe slab rounding or many long-lived small allocations. Any correlation with sequence length or number of KV pages per session?
alice: Correlating session length: sessions > 2500 tokens show 3x higher fragmented_bytes and most of those are streaming sessions with repeated tool invocation. Suspect lifecycle: session creates short-lived temp objects per tool response that allocate buffers which later turn into arena fragmentation.
ben: Could also be KV eviction policy not compacting pages. We use per-shard fixed-size buckets; when entries are freed we mark tombstones but don't physically reclaim until periodic compaction which is rare. Maybe long-lived sessions accumulate tombstones -> fragmentation.
carla: Do we have tombstone metrics?
alice: added metric kv_tombstones_per_shard: median 12, p95 140 on affected pool.
dave: The pool with debug deploy shows GC-like compaction runs every 30m but they are short. We might need adaptive compaction when fragmentation crosses threshold.
ben: Also check whether our KV entries keep a pointer to large buffers (e.g., tool traces) even after logical deletion due to linked structures. A mistyped clear path could hold them.
alice: I grepped code: when Session.Finalize we call cache.Delete(sessionID) but we forgot to call entry.DetachTrace() in the tool loop branch. So the trace slice remains referenced by entry struct until compaction.
carla: Nice catch. That explains stable entry count + resident growth. So it's a logical leak (references held) exacerbating fragmentation.
ben: Action items: 1) hotfix to call DetachTrace on tool completion (PR incoming), 2) instrument tombstone compaction to run when fragmented_bytes > 64MB, 3) improve reuse policy to zero out pointers on delete.
dave: I'm rolling the hotfix to the debug pool now. infra-bot: deploy status: success (10:33 UTC) :rocket:
alice: After hotfix warming (2h) RSS delta looks flat vs previous baseline. Early signs good — growth stopped on the debug pool.
carla: We should still implement adaptive compaction to avoid fragmentation returning under different workloads. Also add unit tests that simulate repeated tool loops.
ben: Agreed. Also schedule a perf run with long streamed tool loops (100 calls) to ensure no regressions.
alice: I'll open tickets: 1) hotfix (attached PR), 2) compaction heuristic, 3) pointer-zeroing on delete, 4) add perf test job.
carla: Can you include a small reproducer script? That would help Ops run in other clusters.
alice: Will add repro: it spins session, loops 60x tool calls with 2KB traces, measures RSS over time, and asserts growth < 5% after 30m.
dave: Thanks team. Leaving this thread open for updates as we roll the compaction piece. :eyes:
